conviction_note: The H1 numbers are new: only Q1 is public (EUR 54.2m, EBIT margin -7.6%). But a widely syndicated Parmantier Sell note on 25 Sep put the H1 bar in public at EUR 140-150m revenue and EBIT around zero, and the stock gave back the whole Energy Vault spike (-10.6% over 24-25 Sep, 65.20 to 58.30). My central case is a print near that whisper, the FY26 guide confirmed and a record-backlog headline, which is how the last three scheduled releases were framed and bought (+7.7%, +6.7%, +7.9%). Against that is a real risk of a guidance trim: hitting the FY guide needs H2 revenue of about EUR 340-350m (+50% y/y) at about 13.5% EBIT margin, and management narrowed at H1 in Sep 2025 and cut in Oct 2025. So abs 7.0 and p_up 55 give +0.7, and the two findings sum to it.

FY26 EUR 490m / 9.5-10.5% most likely confirmed again. There is a real minority risk of the margin range, or less likely revenue, being trimmed given the steep implied H2. Advance payments on the data-center orders are the market's open question (FY25 operating cash flow EUR -38.6m). The balance sheet is expected only with the 15 Oct report, so this probably goes unanswered in the window. Unknown.

findings.finding: The H1 bar was lowered in public four sessions before the print: Parmantier's Sell update, syndicated on EQS, boerse.de, onvista and aktiencheck, told the market to expect H1 revenue of EUR 140-150m and EBIT around zero. The stock then gave back the whole Energy Vault spike (-4.75% on 24 Sep, -6.12% on 25 Sep). A print at or near that whisper, with the guide confirmed and a record backlog, fits the pattern in which this issuer's last three scheduled releases led with orders and closed +6.7% to +7.9% despite weak P&L lines.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Observed on issuer release dates (Yahoo daily closes). 30 Jun 2026 (Q1 EBIT -7.6%, FY25 margin 6.6%, record orders headline): +6.70%. 30 Jul 2026 (order confirmation, guide confirmed): +7.85%. 25 Mar 2026 (FY25 prelim revenue, guide confirmed): +7.68%. But 4 Sep 2025 (H1 report with guide narrowed to lower half): -1.66%.
findings.original_quote: Sehr schwaches erstes Halbjahr erwartet: Umsatz von € 140–150 Mio. (Vorjahr: € 170,3 Mio.), EBIT um die Nulllinie (Translation: very weak first half expected: revenue of EUR 140-150m (prior year EUR 170.3m), EBIT around break-even)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, and that is the point: the down-leg into the print is the market absorbing the weak-H1 whisper, and the price now sits back at 57.75, below where it traded before the Energy Vault order (59.55). If the market still expected a strong H1, the stock would not have round-tripped the order spike on a single sell-side note, and turnover would not have been 69k shares on 25 Sep against a ~40k norm. What is not priced is that the company, not an analyst, confirms the guide two days before its first CMD.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 at EUR 54.2m and -7.6% EBIT margin (company, https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/2g-energy-ag-recorded-by-far-the-highest-order-intake-in-the-companys-history-for-the-quarter-just-ended/53743ee6-af9e-4a1c-9de1-5832812c73c2_en) independently makes a weak H1 arithmetically likely. The positive-reaction pattern comes from price data, not from Parmantier.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide needs a steep H2. At H1 of about EUR 145m and EBIT near zero, EUR 490m and 9.5% need H2 revenue of about EUR 345m (+~50% on H2 2025's ~EUR 228m) at about 13.5% EBIT margin. Management already hedged the margin in May, and it narrowed at the H1 report in Sep 2025 and then cut by ad-hoc in Oct 2025. So a margin or revenue trim in this release is a real minority risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 4 Sep 2025, guide narrowed to lower half at H1: -1.66%. 28-29 Oct 2025, ad-hoc Prognoseanpassung: -3.57% then -3.05% (~-6.5% over two sessions). 26 May 2026, ad-hoc guide to upper end plus FY27 introduced: +21.33%.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side FY26E sits exactly on the guide (First Berlin EUR 490.0m / EBIT 48.3m, 24 Sep), and the Parmantier note attacks cash and the Energy Vault order rather than forecasting a guidance cut. So a trim is not in the published numbers. If it were priced, estimates would sit below the range. The -13% 60-day run-up is ambiguous and also consistent with the H1-weakness finding above.
findings.independence: First Berlin FY26E EBIT 48.3m on 490.0m (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/research/original-research-2g-energy-ag-von-first-berlin-equity-research-gmbh-buy/2c26aadf-7b52-49fc-89dd-034d2dd133c2_de) shows the street is on the guide. The 2025 narrowing is in the company's own 4 Sep 2025 release (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/2g-energy-ag-increases-half-year-output-by-28-eur-193-0-million-previous-year-eur-150-3-million/ed05f1a4-20c6-4c30-a0d9-2cdaf34f6500_en). This finding shares the H1 arithmetic with the first one; the two are opposite branches of one release, not independent evidence.

outside_window.finding: 1st Capital Markets Day in Heek on 1 Oct 2026: mid-term targets (AGM-stated ~20% growth ambition to 2028; FY27 guide possibly lifted for Energy Vault deliveries from Q4 2027). This is more likely the venue for a guidance raise than the 29 Sep prelim.

H1 2026 report with balance sheet on 15 Oct: whether advance payments on the data-center orders arrived. FY25 operating cash flow was EUR -38.6m and net debt EUR 10.2m (via aktiencheck, citing Parmantier). Parmantier expects a capital raise within 12 months, which the company has not announced.

Quality of the Energy Vault 275 MW order. Per Parmantier's reading of NRGV SEC filings, it grew out of a non-binding slot reservation with USD 17.0m of reservation fees disclosed; Energy Vault ordered the same 275 MW from Rolls-Royce MTU with dedicated financing, and had USD 6.9m of stockholders' equity at 30 Jun 2026. Deliveries start Q4 2027.

baseline_tension: The lean is essentially flat (-0.23, all run-up) and there is no short anchor. My slight positive runs against the -4.1% 5-day and -13.3% 60-day tape, on the view that the selloff already absorbed the publicly whispered weak H1. The guidance-trim branch agrees with the tape, which is why the net is small (+0.7) and p_up only 55.
language_note: The only sourced H1 number, Parmantier's EUR 140-150m / EBIT around zero, went out in German first on EQS ('Sehr schwaches erstes Halbjahr erwartet') and was syndicated almost entirely through German portals (boerse.de, onvista, aktiencheck, ad-hoc-news). An English version exists on Parmantier's own CDN, but English wire coverage of it was absent.

First Berlin's German-only research PDF (24 Sep) gave FY26E EUR 490.0m / EBIT 48.3m and the view that H2 order intake will exceed the prior year's ~EUR 120m. That is the only second estimate source I found for the bar.

aktiencheck (German) carried the FY2025 cash-flow facts (operating cash flow EUR +53.3m to -38.6m, net cash EUR 43.1m to net debt EUR 10.2m) that frame the market's advance-payment question. The English company releases do not state them.
The company's own releases and calendar exist on EQS in both languages with identical content, so the English sources carried the event date, the session pattern and the guidance on their own.
lessons_applied: 'Size the move on what is new in the release': H1 revenue and EBIT were never pre-released by the company (only Q1), and a guidance change is live in both directions, so abs_move_pct went from 6.5 to 7.0 (base ~7% for new numbers, 3-7 analyst band, 66% realised vol).

'Let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': the observed release-day reactions (three scheduled releases bought 6.7-7.9% despite weak P&L) nudged p_up from 54 to 55 and the first finding from +1.1 to +1.3. The finding is filed as positioning rather than reported_quarter, because reported_quarter findings went 4 of 14 on sign.

'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': I checked whether the 29 Sep release will answer the advance-payment/cash question. It most likely will not (balance sheet on 15 Oct), so the question stays in outside_window rather than being sized in the window.
'Keep findings inside the exit window': the CMD (1 Oct), the H1 report (15 Oct) and the Energy Vault order quality stay in outside_window, unsized in the sum.
